---
title: "Worked examples"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
# The examples query the live portal, so they are not run when the site is built.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, comment = "#>")
```

Three tasks from start to finish. The same examples are in the
[Python](https://randsley.github.io/dataeuropa/python/examples/) and
[Julia](https://randsley.github.io/dataeuropa/julia/examples/) documentation.

The outputs shown were taken in November 2026. The portal changes all the time, so counts and
search results will differ when you run the code.

## 1. Air quality in Lisbon: from a search to a summary table

Find air-quality data from Portugal that comes as CSV. Quotes make the search match the phrase,
not the separate words.

```{r}
library(dataeuropa)

hits <- de_search_datasets('"air quality"', country = "pt", format = "CSV")
hits[, c("id", "title", "publisher")]
```

```
#>                         id                                         title                  publisher
#> 1 67a5e928a3ee7360b61cd5e4  Sensing: Monthly reports with Air Quality... Câmara Municipal de Oeiras
#> 2 6689f1686e4bd9bc98ed011b  Monitoring of Environmental Parameters o...         Município de Lisboa
```

The Lisbon dataset has one file per period: `QA` files hold air quality, `ME` files weather. List
the files only (no services or web pages):

```{r}
files <- de_distributions("6689f1686e4bd9bc98ed011b", files_only = TRUE)
files[, c("title", "format")]
```

```
#>         title format
#> 1  ME_2024_S1    CSV
#> 2     QA_2023    ZIP
#> ...
#> 6  QA_2024_Q1    CSV
#> ...
```

Read the first quarter of 2024 into a data frame. `de_load_distribution()` takes a row of the
table and checks the file's checksum when the portal has one.

```{r}
qa <- de_load_distribution(files[files$title == "QA_2024_Q1", ])
head(qa[, c("DTM_LOCAL", "PARAMETRO", "LOCAL", "UNIDADE", "VALOR")], 3)
```

```
#>               DTM_LOCAL PARAMETRO            LOCAL UNIDADE VALOR
#> 1 2024-01-05 19:00:00.0      PM25 Calçada da Ajuda   µg/m3     6
#> 2 2024-01-06 03:00:00.0      PM25 Calçada da Ajuda   µg/m3     5
#> 3 2024-01-06 04:00:00.0      PM25 Calçada da Ajuda   µg/m3     3
```

The file is in long format: one row per reading, with the pollutant in `PARAMETRO`. `-99` marks a
missing reading. Some stations have only a few readings, so count them too and keep the stations
with at least 300 before comparing NO₂ means:

```{r}
no2 <- qa[qa$PARAMETRO == "NO2" & qa$VALOR >= 0, ]
by_station <- data.frame(mean = tapply(no2$VALOR, no2$LOCAL, mean),
                         count = tapply(no2$VALOR, no2$LOCAL, length))
by_station <- by_station[by_station$count >= 300, ]
head(round(by_station[order(-by_station$mean), ], 1), 5)
```

```
#>                                    mean count
#> Avenida António Augusto de Aguiar 111.9   356
#> Campo de Ourique                   95.3   356
#> Praça São Francisco de Assis       93.9   356
#> Rua Morais Soares                  92.0   356
#> Estrada de Monsanto                78.0   356
```

Without the count filter, a station with 35 readings (one of them 564) would come first.

## 2. Who publishes air-quality data, and in what formats

Counts and facets need no records, so they are fast (and cached when `de_cache_on()` is set).

```{r}
de_count('"air quality"')                              # 3583
de_facet_values("country", '"air quality"', top = 8)
```

```
#>       id          label count
#> 1 EUROPE         Europe   621
#> 2     de        Germany   538
#> 3     fr         France   449
#> 4     gb United Kingdom   372
#> 5     es          Spain   347
#> 6     it          Italy   247
#> 7     ro        Romania   189
#> 8     bg       Bulgaria   147
```

`EUROPE` is the value for datasets about Europe as a whole. Formats:

```{r}
de_facet_values("format", '"air quality"', top = 6)
```

```
#>         id label count
#> 1      CSV   CSV   868
#> 2     JSON  JSON   536
#> 3      XML   XML   391
#> 4 WMS_SRVC   WMS   245
#> 5      ZIP   ZIP   172
#> 6     HTML  HTML   145
```

Use the `id` column in filters: `de_search_datasets('"air quality"', format = "WMS_SRVC")`. A
dataset with several formats counts once for each, so format counts can add up to more than the
total.

## 3. Boundaries of Gelsenkirchen from a feature service

The city of Gelsenkirchen publishes its administrative boundaries as a GeoServer service, which
the portal lists as OGC API Features and as WFS. This needs the sf package
(`install.packages("sf")`).

```{r}
dists <- de_distributions("eac1e504-9d63-4670-95b3-3ef04e22aa6e~~1")
dists[, c("format", "kind")]
```

```
#>     format    kind
#> 1  OGCFEAT service
#> 2     JSON    file
#> 3 WFS_SRVC service
```

The OGC API Features entry points to one collection, the cadastral districts. The data comes in
ETRS89 / UTM zone 32N (EPSG:25832), which is in metres, so areas can be computed directly:

```{r}
districts <- de_load_geodata(dists[dists$format == "OGCFEAT", ])
districts$area_km2 <- round(as.numeric(sf::st_area(districts)) / 1e6, 2)
head(sf::st_drop_geometry(districts)[order(-districts$area_km2), c("gemarkung_name", "area_km2")], 3)
```

```
#>    gemarkung_name area_km2
#> 6            Buer    61.29
#> 5        Bismarck    10.08
#> 10         Heßler     6.88
```

The WFS entry is the whole service, with 22 layers. Without `layer`, `de_load_geodata()` reads the
first and lists them all in a message. Pick the city quarters by name; the namespace prefix
(`verwaltungsgrenzen:`) can be left out. `crs` reprojects, here to longitude and latitude:

```{r}
quarters <- de_load_geodata(dists[dists$format == "WFS_SRVC", ], layer = "stadtteil", crs = "EPSG:4326")
nrow(quarters)                                         # 18
plot(sf::st_geometry(quarters))
```

Services can be large, so `de_load_geodata()` reads at most 10,000 features and warns when there
are more. Pass `max_features = Inf` to read all of them.
